title: How long is each part of the two crossing strips?
description: The two diagonals of a rectangle cross at O, and one diagonal is eight centimetres. Two congruent triangles show that O cuts each diagonal in half, and Keeko then asks whether anyone really builds rectangles with this method.
teaching_notes: One idea: the diagonals of a rectangle cut each other into equal halves, shown by two congruent triangles at the crossing. Watch for students who stop at the first diagonal and forget that the second diagonal is equal to it.

source: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and AC = 8 cm. Fin
video_script.why: The child sees that the crossing point of the diagonals of a rectangle is the midpoint of both, which is the second half of the method for making a rectangle.
video_script.substitution: Name the crossing as O, pick the two triangles AOB and COD, match them by AAS, and read off the four parts.
video_script.anchor: rectangle ABCD with its diagonals AC and BD crossing at O, and AC labelled 8 cm
video_script.payoff_line: Each of the four parts is four centimetres long

final_answer.spoken: each of the four parts is four centimetres long

maths_rules: ABCD is a rectangle, the diagonals AC and BD meet at O, and AC = 8 cm
in triangle AOB and triangle COD: AB = CD (opposite sides of a rectangle)
angle AOB = angle COD (vertically opposite angles)
angle ABO = 90 degrees minus angle OBC, and angle CDO = 90 degrees minus angle OBC (triangle BCD has a right angle at C), so angle ABO = angle CDO
AAS: triangle AOB is congruent to triangle COD, so OA = OC and OB = OD
BD = AC = 8 cm (diagonals of a rectangle are equal)
OA = OC = 8 / 2 = 4 cm and OB = OD = 8 / 2 = 4 cm
video_script.design: One idea: the diagonals of a rectangle meet at the midpoint of each. The real life ending is the carpenters of Europe and the farmers of Mozambique from the chapter text.
